Book 18 of the Analects, 微子 Wēi zǐ, named, as every book is, from its first words — the Viscount of Wei, half-brother of the last Shang king, who left his tyrannical lord rather than serve him. The Analects is a collection of short sayings and exchanges of Confucius (Kǒngzǐ, 551–479 BC) and his disciples, put together by their followers over several generations; the twenty books were not composed as a whole, and nothing in them was written down by Confucius himself. Book 18 has 11 passages, and Zhu Xi says it mostly records when sages and worthies took office and when they withdrew. It opens with three men who answered a bad king in three ways — leaving, enduring slavery, dying for their protest — and Kongzi calls all three humane (18.1). Liuxia Hui, dismissed three times, will not leave his own state (18.2); Kongzi leaves Qi when its duke will not use him, and leaves Lu when its chief minister takes a gift of women musicians and holds no court (18.3–4). Then come the recluses who mock him: the madman of Chu singing to the phoenix (18.5); two men ploughing who will not tell Zilu where the ford is, and Kongzi's answer that he cannot go off to live among the birds and beasts (18.6); and an old man, a bamboo basket slung from the staff on his shoulder, who answers Zilu's question with a gibe — 'who is your master?' — and then gives him a night's lodging (18.7). Seven men of worth who lived out of office are named, the Master passes judgment on six of them, two by two, and says he himself has no fixed 'may' or 'may not' (18.8). The book ends with the musicians of Lu scattering to other states, to the River and to the sea (18.9), the Duke of Zhou's counsel to his son (18.10), and eight officers of Zhou, four pairs of brothers (18.11). Each numbered passage begins a new card; longer passages are cut where Zhu Xi's commentary interrupts the text. The original has no punctuation: every comma, quotation mark and full stop is an editor's interpretation. Read the characters; the pinyin under each one is a reading aid you can hide with the transcription button.
